rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday verb for taking a measurement such as temperature, blood pressure, or length.

example.english: Let me measure your blood pressure first.
example.jyutping: ngo5 bong1 nei5 loeng4 haa5 hyut3 aat3 sin1

rows.note: Use this especially for measuring temperature or taking a body measurement, where 度 is a common alternative to 量.

example.jyutping: nei5 bong1 ngo5 dok6 haa5 tai2 wan1

rows.note: Use this for deliberate or technical measuring, especially surveying or measuring physical dimensions.

example.english: The engineer needs to measure the length of this wall.
example.traditional: 工程師要測量呢幅牆嘅長度。
example.jyutping: gung1 cing4 si1 jiu3 caak1 loeng4 ni1 fuk1 coeng4 ge3 coeng4 dou6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when “measure” means a standard or criterion for judging something.

example.jyutping: ni1 go3 sin1 hai6 gung1 ping4 ge3 biu1 zeon2

rows.note: Use this construction to say that something is of a particular size or area.

example.english: The living room is big enough to measure 300 square feet.
example.traditional: 個廳有三百平方呎咁大。
example.jyutping: go3 teng1 jau5 saam1 baak3 ping4 fong1 cek3 gam3 daai6

rows.note: Use this for a unit such as a gram, metre, or other measurement unit.

example.english: A metre is a unit of measure for length.
example.jyutping: mai5 hai6 coeng4 dou6 ge3 daan1 wai2

rows.note: Use this when “measure” means the amount or portion of something dealt out, rather than the vessel itself.

example.english: The measure of soup in this bowl is just right.
example.jyutping: ni1 wun2 tong1 ge3 fan6 loeng6 ngaam1 ngaam1 hou2

rows.note: Use this for an ordinary straight ruler or measuring stick; a tape measure is normally named more specifically.

example.english: Lend me a ruler so I can measure the table.
example.traditional: 借把間尺畀我度下張枱。
example.jyutping: ze3 baa2 gaan1 cek3 bei2 ngo5 dou6 haa5 zoeng1 toi2
